sender.en: A Facebook, Instagram or TikTok page selling phones, electronics or cars cheap

name.en: Fake online seller: “advance payment by JazzCash or Easypaisa first, then delivery”

how.en: A page on Facebook, Instagram or TikTok advertises phones, appliances or even cars far below market price, often with a countdown or “last few pieces”. The seller asks for full or advance payment by JazzCash, Easypaisa or bank transfer before sending. After payment the item never arrives, a different item arrives, or the seller asks for more money for “delivery” and then blocks you. NCCIA warned about these sellers ahead of the 11.11 sales.

text.en: A social media ad shows a big discount on a costly item.
The offer ends “in minutes” or stock is “almost finished”.
You must pay in advance by JazzCash, Easypaisa or transfer.
After payment they ask for more or block you.
iPhone 15 Pro Max sirf 65,000 mein! Sirf 3 piece baqi. Pehle advance payment Easypaisa karein, order kal tak deliver ho jayega.
Sir parcel dispatch ho gaya hai lekin courier charges 3,500 aur insurance pending hai, JazzCash kar dein warna parcel wapas chala jayega.

en: facebook page took advance payment and blocked me
online order paid easypaisa never delivered
advance payment ke baad block kar diya
cheap iphone ad on facebook scam
seller asked more money for delivery charges
tiktok shop fake seller jazzcash payment
non custom paid car ad advance payment scam
Advance payment only, no cash on delivery.
Prefer cash on delivery or a marketplace’s own payment; check reviews and the page’s history.
Keep screenshots, receipts and the ad.
Report to NCCIA on 1799 or its portal, and tell your bank or wallet at once.

sources.title: 11.11 Mega Sale Alert: Pakistanis warned against Fake Discounts, Online Scammers

story.en: A buyer who saw Facebook and Instagram ads for non-customs-paid vehicles at half the market price paid upfront for delivery. The sellers kept asking for more money, and he lost Rs 100,000.
